document.title: Can DNA Act as an Information Storage Medium? A Serviceability-First Archival Research Proposal

source_controls.discovery_method: OpenAlex and AnySearch Academic dual-engine search with DOI-based cross-validation where records overlap.

browser_metadata_check.verified_record: Church, Gao, and Kosuri, Next-Generation Digital Information Storage in DNA, Science, 16 August 2012, volume 337 issue 6102, page 1628

source_controls.human_review_required: Verify publisher or full-text methodological applicability for every cited source before real wet-lab work, deployment, or scholarly submission.

claim_boundary.supported_conclusion: DNA is a proven digital information medium, while archive usefulness depends on a declared end-to-end service envelope rather than ideal molecular density alone.
not_claimed: a newly executed DNA synthesis, storage, sequencing, simulation, or benchmark
replacement of RAM, SSDs, or active cloud databases
living-cell, clinical, or environmental DNA storage
